dropped.1: Pre-release: ConsoleShellProps lost its `error` field. The announced role="alert" banner is `<SessionErrorBanner>` now — its own export, COMPOSED inside ConsoleShell — so a full-bleed chrome can take the announced-error decision without taking the frame. Epoch 1's `<ConsoleShell error={session.error?.message} …>` no longer compiles; the migration is to delete that prop, since the shell renders the banner itself. `BulletList`, `Facts` and `SessionErrorBanner` join the capability in the same move.
dropped.2: Purely ADDITIVE: useFlash/useCopy and their named result types UseFlashResult/UseCopyResult join the capability, so every epoch-2 declaration compiles unchanged. Dropped rather than retained because this package retains no superseded epoch — with no external consumers a frozen example would be a promise about a surface nobody holds, which is why contracts/compatibility/ does not exist here. What moved: three hand-rolled copies of the one-live-timer, clear-on-unmount flash (the studio's editor save note, its copy buttons, and this package's own components/url-chips.tsx) became one primitive. The url-chips copy was the worst of the three — it ended `.catch(() => {})`, so on an insecure context or a denied permission the button visibly did nothing; a refusal reports "Failed" now. They are in components rather than hooks because that capability promises what a client reads off the AGENT, and these read nothing and render nothing — they are the same category as AutoScroll, a behaviour rule a custom chrome would otherwise re-derive.

What moved: the control-selection rule was extracted out of SchemaField (components/workflow-fields.tsx) so there is ONE decision, and published because it is not derivable by inspection — an upload property IS a plain string in the schema, so the ORDER (upload, then enum, then type) is invisible to a reader. The studio's API pane was carrying a hand-kept mirror of that switch, with a comment admitting it and a test pinning the order to catch the drift; it reads the rule now, so a new control reaches its docs table as a widened union rather than as an edit somebody has to remember. It is in forms rather than components because what it names is a FIELD: adding a control to <WorkflowFields> widens WorkflowFieldKind, so the two move together and one epoch covers both halves.

dropped.1: Pre-release: DEFAULT_PROGRESS_POLL_MS, DEFAULT_WORKFLOW_POLL_MS and MAX_MISSING_READS moved to @alexkroman1/aai-ui/internal. All three are tuning numbers referenced by no public signature and named by no file outside this package; the hooks that own them take the interval as an OPTION, which is the authoring surface for the same choice and stays public.
dropped.2: The workflow hooks' type parameter is the workflow DEFINITION, not its output type. Epoch 2's `useWorkflowSubmit<Digest>("digest")` no longer compiles: the parameter is constrained to `AnyWorkflowDef`, deliberately, so passing an output type is a compile error rather than a silent loss of typing. What it buys is the other half of the contract — `submit(input)` was `unknown`, so `submit({ ur1: 42 })` compiled and arrived as a 400 in the browser while the same statement already derived the OUTPUT from the def. Migration is one token per call site: `<Digest>` becomes `<typeof digest>`, and the `WorkflowOutputOf` alias above it is deleted.
dropped.3: The workflow hooks' def type parameter is REQUIRED — there is no `unknown` fallback for an un-parameterized call. It existed so `useWorkflowSubmit("digest")` kept compiling, and it was the last way to get an untyped `submit` back. A workflow that declares no input schema now gets `submit(): void` rather than an unusable `never` parameter.
dropped.4: Pre-release: the SDK has no external consumers, so no superseded authoring style is owed a compiling example. A workflow that declares no input schema gets `submit(undefined)` rather than `submit()`: `void` would let the argument be omitted, and Biome's `noConfusingVoidType` rejects it outside a return or type-parameter position.
dropped.5: Pre-release: `SubmitInputOf` and `WorkflowInputOf` are ADDED to the barrel, so this epoch would in fact still compile. Dropped rather than retained because this package has no external consumers and contracts/compatibility/ stays empty. `SubmitInputOf` is in both submit hooks' return type and had nowhere to click; `WorkflowInputOf` was the missing half of a pair whose other half was already re-exported here. `SubmitOutputOf` came off in the same change — it was `WorkflowOutputOf` spelled a second way.
dropped.6: `useRunKey` is purely additive, but `UseWorkflowStreamOptions` narrowed in the same change to `Omit<UseWorkflowSubmitOptions, "wait" | "recover">` — so epoch 6 client code that passed `recover` to a stream submit no longer compiles. No external consumer exists to keep an epoch-6 template for, and aai-ui has dropped every prior epoch on the same grounds.

dropped.9: Parameter names only (API parameter naming review, part 2): the options bag is `options` everywhere it was `opts`, plus the per-signature fixes that review found — `WorkflowClient.get` and `EvalWorkflows.settle` take `workflow` rather than the preposition `of`, `LogFn` takes `message`, `RuntimeOptions.onToolResult` takes `message`, `ServerSession.command` takes `command`, `ClientSink.event` takes `event`, `registerChannelHandler` takes `handler` rather than `kind` (its argument is the whole handler, not a tag), `responseErrorMessage` takes `response`, `createRunSnapshot` takes `overrides`, `mapConcurrent` takes `width` (the module doc distinguishes the window from the concurrency), `stepTranscribePoll` takes `transcriptId` (it is not the `uploadId` its neighbour takes), `slugifyName` takes `(name, maxLength)`, `decodeWorkspaceText` takes `bytes`, and the eval mode gates take `hostEnv` like the credential readers they delegate to. No export, signature type or behaviour moved, and TypeScript parameters are positional, so the superseded epoch compiles unchanged — but the names are in the report, so the hash moves. Dropped rather than retained for the reason every such entry here gives: with no external consumers a frozen example would be evidence for a promise nobody holds.
